_comment: THE BATCH THAT CANNOT RUN ON THIS PROJECT'S MACHINE, written so the route
exists the day a qualifying one does, and so the refusal is about a real
batch rather than a hypothetical.
microsoft/TRELLIS README, read 2026-09-01: 'An NVIDIA GPU with at least
16GB of memory is necessary', the CUDA Toolkit 'is needed to compile
certain submodules', and 'The code is currently tested only on Linux'
(Windows is issue #3, 'not fully tested'). Jafar's PC is an AMD Radeon RX
6700 with 9.98 GB and no Visual Studio at all. Four blockers, each
sufficient alone. meshgen.py --command probe prints all four with the
measured value beside each.
TARGET HEIGHTS ARE REQUIRED HERE AND ABSENT FROM THE LOCAL BATCH, and the
difference is not style: TRELLIS output is normalised into a unit cube, so
it has no scale at all until one is given. Each number below is the
real-world size of the object named, and the pipeline measures the export
afterwards so a wrong one shows up as a bound rather than as a belief.
LICENCE, AND IT IS NOT SETTLED. The allowlist says TRELLIS is MIT. TRELLIS
says 'models and the majority of the code' are MIT and names submodules
that are not (diffoctreerast, derived from INRIA diff-gaussian-
rasterization; modified FlexiCubes under an NVIDIA source licence). Until a
decision record names which of those the mesh path loads, every row this
batch produces is tagged ship_ok=false with that sentence attached.
